protocol.justification: Prospectively test half and double the retained 100 km cutoff, equally spaced on a logarithmic scale, as a finite-boundary convergence/stress diagnostic. These analyst settings are not source-supported regional vegetation extents, field observations, probabilities or fitted choices. Retain negligible, adverse and refused outcomes.
protocol.support_policy: preserve exact original case/window/taxon/count/PPE/age support; no new samples, cross-window uncertainty or independent-site pooling

reference_scope: The unchanged public baseline retains native counts, ages, literal parameter panels, PPE/SD, geometry and baseline moments. Exact case hashes and ordered window hashes bind those records. The separately pinned native report retains every alternative moment and its signed alternative-minus-saved-100-km difference; this compact account does not copy those arrays.
limits: Saved K is source-qualified, not independently recomputed for these 46 cutoff tuples. Conditional count and diagonal-PPE delta moments only. The 50 km and 200 km cutoffs are declared numerical stress settings around 100 km, not measured or source-supported regional extents, empirical likelihoods or a plausible-range distribution. There is no proof of asymptotic convergence to an infinite region, cross-window uncertainty, chronology or shoreline calibration, independent-site pooling, field accuracy, source-use permission, human review or whole LCI-030 acceptance.
development_exposure: The saved 100 km Nordic baseline, the existing Swedish assumptions and the prior Nordic wind results were exposed before this finite cutoff protocol; this is conditional development sensitivity, not untouched confirmation.
